To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new cyclopentadine ligands were synthesized and the rhodium complexes with these ligands were prepared.
we have synthesized a new class of cyclopentadiene ligands with perfluoroalky substituents.

(perfluoro)alkyl-substituted tetramethylcyclo-pentadienes have been synthesized and characterized by combination GC-MS and NMR spectroscopy, and rhodium(III) and rhodium(I), complexes have been prepared and characterized by spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general strategy for the preparation of a series of novel perfluoroalkane substituted cyclopentadiene complexes of rhodium.
the synthesis, characterization, and application of perfluoroalkyldicarbonyl complexes of rhodium(I) with novel (perfluoro-alkyl)tetra-methylcyclopentadienide ligands.
the synthesis of new cyclopenta-1-ylidene ligands for organometallic complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perfluorinated cyclopentadiene ligands are electronically similar to cyclopentadienylderivatives and that the electronic effects of the substituents on the cyclopentenyl ring are small.
the perfluoro-alkyl chain is not a good electronic or steric substituent for the cyclopentadine ligand.
the electronic effects of perfluoroalkylation of cyclopentadiene are small and can be neglected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new perfluoroalkylylated cyclopentadiene ligands are electronically similar to the unsubstitued cyclopentadienylderived ligands.
the perfluoro alkyl chain has no significant influence on the properties of the cyclopentenyl ligands and the corresponding rhodium complexes.
these new cyclopentenyl ligands are not significantly different from the cyclopenta-dienyl ligands in their coordination to rhodium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the perfluoro-substituted ligands are electronically similar to the cyclopentadientyl ligand, and the complexes are stable in air, which makes them suitable candidates for catalysis in fluoroorganic media.
perfluoroalkylation of cyclopentadiene with a perfluorinated carboxylic acid is an efficient way for synthesis of perfluoroalkane-substituted cyclopenta-1,3-diene ligands.
the perfluorinated cyclopentadiene ligands can be used for synthesis of rhodium complexes in the same manner as the unsubstituted ligand.
